chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from one of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who sold merchandise to another man, and the buyer took possession of the merchandise but did not pay the price, then the buyer died while the merchandise was still intact in its very form,
So he عليه السلام said: “If the merchandise remains intact in its very form, it is to be returned to the owner of the merchandise, and the creditors have no right to dispute with him over it.”

key_terms.الثَّمَنَ: the sale price owed for the merchandise
key_terms.الْغُرَمَاءِ: the creditors who are owed debts
key_terms.الْمُشْتَرِي: the buyer who took possession of the goods
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْمَتَاعِ: the owner of the merchandise, meaning the seller here
key_terms.قَائِمٌ بِعَيْنِهِ: remaining intact in its original identifiable form
key_terms.يُخَاصِمُوهُ: to dispute or litigate against him over the item

ai.seo_question: If a buyer dies before paying for goods that are still intact, do the creditors have any claim over them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about sold merchandise when the buyer dies before paying its price. If the item still exists unchanged, it returns to the seller, and the deceased buyer’s creditors cannot claim it as part of the estate. The report is significant in financial law for determining ownership and creditor rights in cases of unpaid sale transactions.
